lede: Luxury's H1 earnings season closes with a hard-vs-soft divergence verdict, the EU AI Act's content-labelling teeth bite down, and Lyst's first AI-native index reshapes how brand heat is measured — all in a week that demands both a compliance audit and a data strategy reset.

stories.headline: Lyst Embeds AI Discovery Channels Into Q2 2026 Index — Chanel Holds No. 1 as Methodology Gets a Machine-Learning Upgrade
stories.summary: Lyst published its Q2 2026 Index on August 5, tracking 160 million annual shoppers across searches, sales, social, editorial — and, for the first time at scale, AI-powered discovery channels. Chanel held the top spot for the second consecutive quarter, driven by Coco Beach and Métiers d'Art collections plus a 70% jump in sunglasses demand; Miu Miu climbed to No. 2 on a 30% demand surge. The methodology update is the real signal: brand heat is now measured across LLM recommendation surfaces, meaning luxury houses that aren't optimising for AI citation will begin to disappear from the index.

stories.headline: EU AI Act Article 50 Is Live — Synthetic Content Labelling Enforcement Begins Across All 27 Member States
stories.summary: On August 2, 2026, the EU AI Act's transparency obligations under Article 50 became enforceable: any AI-generated or AI-manipulated image, video, audio, or text deployed in the EU must now carry machine-readable synthetic-content markers, with fines of up to €15M or 3% of global turnover for breaches. High-risk system obligations were deferred to December 2027 via the Digital Omnibus, but the labelling deadline was explicitly left untouched — meaning every luxury maison running generative AI campaign assets is now in live enforcement territory. The Commission's GPAI supervisory powers also switched on the same day.

stories.headline: Luxury's H1 Recovery Has a Value-for-Money Problem — LVMH, Kering and Hermès Return to Growth, But Jewellery Is Carrying Everyone
stories.summary: H1 2026 results across the major conglomerates confirmed a structural divergence: LVMH's Watches & Jewellery grew 11% in Q2 while Fashion & Leather only just returned to positive territory at +1% after seven consecutive down quarters; Kering's jewellery grew 18% against a flat fashion division; Richemont's jewellery maisons posted a seventh straight quarter of double-digit growth. Glossy's analysis, drawing on commentary from Bernstein analyst Luca Solca, frames the gap as a value-for-money crisis — entry-price jewellery now offers a more defensible price-to-quality ratio than handbags whose prices have risen steeply since 2019. Brands that built their P&L on leather goods must now rebuild the product logic that once justified the premium.

stories.headline: Prada Group Posts 22nd Consecutive Quarter of Organic Growth — China Recovers, Versace Weighs on Profit
stories.summary: Prada Group closed H1 2026 with net revenue of €3.048 billion, up 16% at constant exchange rates, with organic growth accelerating to 7% in Q2 — a performance that continues to widen the group's gap with peers. Chinese customers delivered double-digit growth in Q2, with domestic and overseas spend recovering in tandem, while the Prada brand's retail sales grew 6.3% in the quarter on full-price, like-for-like momentum. The drag: Versace, acquired late last year, weighed on group profitability, with net profit falling 15.2% to €327M as acquisition amortisation and currency effects bit.

stories.headline: Rokt Launches Brain V4 — Real-Time AI Decisioning at Checkout Reaches 10 Billion Transactions in 2026
stories.summary: Rokt launched Brain V4 on August 4, a reengineered AI core that determines in real time what a customer sees during the Transaction Moment — the point of purchase completion — drawing on customer, advertiser, contextual, and transactional data simultaneously, including the option to show nothing at all. The platform is on track to power over 10 billion transactions in 2026 across partners including Macy's, Ulta Beauty, PayPal, and Fanatics. For luxury media buyers, the signal is structural: as agentic AI compresses the top of the funnel, checkout is becoming the last human-controlled interaction — and the performance layer sitting inside it is now AI-native.
